episodes.title: Welcome to Chandamama — Uncle Moon's Story House
episodes.subtitle: A warm introduction to the magical world of Chandamama

cast.name: Uncle Moonbeam
cast.description: The kindly moon uncle who tells stories to children across the world.

scenes.title: The Moonlit Terrace
scenes.setting: A soft silver terrace under a full moon, with cushions scattered about and a warm lantern glowing.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Hello, my little stars! I am Uncle Moonbeam, and welcome to my Story House.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Long, long ago, in the year nineteen forty-seven, a magical magazine was born in the land of India.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: It was called Chandamama. That means 'Moon Uncle' in the language of Telugu.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Every month, children across the subcontinent would wait eagerly for Chandamama to arrive. It came in Sanskrit, in Telugu, in Hindi, in Tamil, in Bengali, and in so many more tongues.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The stories carried ancient wisdom. Lessons of dharma — doing what is right. Of ahimsa — kindness to all living things. And of courage that comes in all sizes.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Now, from the December nineteen ninety-nine Sanskrit issue, preserved carefully on Archive dot org, we are bringing these tales back to life.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: As free podcasts. As interactive storybooks. In eight languages. For children everywhere.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: So snuggle up, little traveler. The moon is full, the stars are bright, and the stories are about to begin. Are you ready?

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Then let us begin with our first tale. But first, a little puzzle for you. Look at the moon tonight. Can you see the face of the old man in the moon? He is smiling at you. Goodnight, little stars. Until we meet again.

episodes.title: The King and the Queen — A Royal Mystery
episodes.subtitle: From the cover of the December 1999 issue: What does the King see?

cast.name: Uncle Moonbeam
cast.description: The kindly storyteller who guides us through the tale.

cast.name: King Vikramaditya
cast.description: A wise and just king who sees something extraordinary on the horizon.

cast.name: Queen Ananya
cast.description: The curious and kind queen who listens with wonder.

cast.name: Minister Gopal
cast.description: The king's trusted advisor, cautious but clever.

scenes.title: The Royal Balcony at Dawn
scenes.setting: The king and queen stand on a marble balcony as the first rays of sun paint the sky in gold and saffron.

scenes.title: The Throne Room
scenes.setting: A grand hall with pillars of sandstone, where the court gathers to discuss the king's vision.

scenes.title: The Garden of Answers
scenes.setting: A moonlit garden where the queen discovers the truth hidden among the jasmine flowers.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: In the ancient kingdom of Ujjain, there lived a king named Vikramaditya. He was known throughout the land for his wisdom, his justice, and his kindness to all creatures great and small.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: One crisp winter morning, as the first rays of dawn painted the sky in gold and saffron, the king stood upon his royal balcony, gazing far into the eastern hills.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: My dear Ananya, come quickly! Look there, beyond the seven hills. Do you see what I see?

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: What is it, my lord? I see only the morning mist rolling over the hills... wait. Is that... a light? A golden light, dancing upon the highest peak?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: Yes! It is no ordinary light. It pulses like a heartbeat. I believe it is the Lamp of Dharma, lost for three hundred years.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: The Lamp of Dharma? But my lord, that is only a legend told to children at bedtime. Are you certain?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: I am as certain as the sun rising in the east. And if it is indeed the Lamp, we must send a expedition at once. For whoever holds the Lamp of Dharma holds the wisdom to rule justly for a thousand years.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The king called his court to the throne room. Ministers, scholars, and soldiers gathered, their whispers filling the grand hall like the rustle of autumn leaves.

script.speaker: Minister Gopal
script.text: Your Majesty, with respect, the eastern hills are treacherous. The path is guarded by old forests where even brave men lose their way. And the mountain peak is said to be cursed.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: Cursed? Nonsense, Gopal. The only curse is the fear in our own hearts. But you are right about the danger. That is why I shall go myself.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: You, my lord? But the kingdom needs you here!

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: The kingdom needs wisdom more than it needs a king who sits safely on his throne. Besides, I will not go alone. I will take only those who volunteer — and a good supply of courage.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The queen could see that her husband's mind was set firm as the mountain itself. So she devised a plan of her own.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Then I volunteer, my lord. For where you go, I go. And I know a secret path through the eastern forest — a path shown to me by my grandmother, who was a forest healer.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so, dear listeners, the king and queen set out at dawn the very next day. But that, my little stars, is a story for another moonlit night. For now, remember this: the greatest treasures are not found in distant hills, but in the courage to seek them, and in the love of those who walk beside us. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Dr. Rabbit's Puzzle — A Maze Adventure
episodes.subtitle: Help Smita find her way to the dentist through a magical maze!

cast.name: Smita
cast.description: A bright and brave little girl who must find her way through the maze.

cast.name: Dr. Rabbit
cast.description: A clever rabbit who is also the best dentist in the forest.

scenes.title: Smita's Village
scenes.setting: A sunny village with colorful houses, where Smita is playing with her friends.

scenes.title: The Whispering Woods
scenes.setting: A friendly forest where the trees seem to point the way, and butterflies form arrows in the air.

scenes.title: Dr. Rabbit's Burrow
scenes.setting: A cozy underground clinic with carrot-shaped chairs and a warm fireplace.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: In a little village where the houses were painted in every color of the rainbow, there lived a girl named Smita. She was six years old, brave as a lion cub, and curious as a kitten.

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: Smita, my little sunshine, it is time for your visit to Dr. Rabbit. Remember, he lives on the other side of the Whispering Woods.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: But Mama, the Whispering Woods are so big! What if I get lost?

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: You won't get lost, my brave girl. Dr. Rabbit left a puzzle for you. If you solve it, the path will open like a flower. Here, look at this map.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Smita looked at the map. It was no ordinary map. It was a maze! A beautiful, winding maze drawn in carrot ink on birch bark.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: I see three paths! The red path goes through the Thorny Thicket. The blue path crosses the Bubbling Brook. And the green path winds through the Butterfly Meadow. Which one is right, Mama?

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: Dr. Rabbit's note says: 'Choose the path where friends help friends, where flowers smile, and where the water sings.'

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Friends help friends... flowers smile... water sings... I know! The green path through Butterfly Meadow! Butterflies are friends to flowers, and the meadow has a singing stream!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so Smita set off, her little boots crunching on the forest path. The Whispering Woods were not scary at all — they were whispering encouragement! 'You can do it, little one,' rustled the leaves.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Hello, Mr. Squirrel! Have you seen Dr. Rabbit's burrow?

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The squirrel chattered and dropped an acorn right on a mossy stone that had an arrow carved into it. 'Follow the acorns!' seemed to be the message.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Thank you, Mr. Squirrel! I will follow the acorns!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: At last, Smita reached a round green door with a carrot-shaped knocker. She knocked three times.

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: Well, well, well! If it isn't little Smita! I see you solved my puzzle. The green path of friendship and kindness. That is always the right path, you know.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: I did it, Dr. Rabbit! And the woods helped me. The squirrel showed me the way, and the butterflies danced me across the meadow!

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: That is because you have a kind heart, Smita. Kind hearts always find their way. Now, let us look at those teeth. Open wide and say 'ahhh'!

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Ahhhh!

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: Perfect! Strong and shiny, just like your courage. Here is a carrot for being the bravest patient of the day. And remember, brush twice a day — morning and night!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so, dear little listeners, Smita walked home with a carrot in her hand, a smile on her face, and a new lesson in her heart: when you are kind and brave, the whole world helps you find your way. Now, who is ready to draw their own maze? Goodnight, little stars!
